ip_top_stories.title: Court of Justice asked to clarify copyright rules for AI training and chatbot outputs
ip_top_stories.summary: The Court of Justice of the European Union has been asked to clarify how copyright rules apply to AI training data and the outputs generated by AI chatbots. The referral seeks to establish clearer legal boundaries for AI developers and rights holders across EU member states.

ip_top_stories.title: Universal and Sony Want Suno's Newest AI Models Exposed in 60K-Recording Copyright Battle
ip_top_stories.summary: Universal Music Group and Sony Music are demanding that Suno's newest AI music generation models be subjected to discovery in the ongoing copyright lawsuit involving approximately 60,000 recordings. The labels argue that examining the new models is essential to understanding the full scope of alleged infringement.

ip_top_stories.title: Reservoir Widens AI Copyright Suits Against Suno and Anthropic to Over 2,500 Songs
ip_top_stories.summary: Music rights company Reservoir has expanded its AI copyright lawsuits against both Suno and Anthropic, now covering more than 2,500 songs. The expansion signals a broadening litigation front from music publishers targeting both AI music generation and large language model developers.

ip_top_stories.title: Court allows news publishers' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI to go ahead
ip_top_stories.summary: A court has permitted a copyright lawsuit brought by news publishers against OpenAI to proceed, marking a significant development in the ongoing legal battles over the use of journalistic content to train large language models. The ruling allows publishers to pursue their claims that OpenAI reproduced their material without authorisation or compensation.

ip_top_stories.title: Getty v Stability AI appeal: BPI backs Getty in UK court
ip_top_stories.summary: The British Phonographic Industry has filed a submission supporting Getty Images in its UK appeal against Stability AI, broadening the coalition of rights holders challenging AI image generation companies. The intervention underlines growing cross-industry concern about AI training on copyrighted material under UK law.

ip_further_links.title: ByteDance sued by automotive photography firm EVOX, alleging TikTok parent copied 7,095 images to train its Seedream AI image generator
ip_further_links.summary: Automotive image library EVOX has filed suit against ByteDance alleging that 7,095 of its photographs were copied without authorisation to train the Seedream AI image generation model.

ip_further_links.title: The Anatomy of
: An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult discusses how AI threatens rights holders' revenues, the limitations of opt-out frameworks, and what meaningful licensing for AI training should look like.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Beyond the Download: What Counts as Scholarly Content Use in the Age of AI?
ip_further_links.summary: A Scholarly Kitchen guest post examines how traditional metrics of content use fail to capture AI-driven consumption of scholarly material, raising new questions for publishers and rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: 'Deeply flawed': Former ACCC boss slams opt-out AI copyright plan
ip_further_links.summary: Australia's former competition regulator chief has criticised proposed opt-out AI copyright arrangements as deeply flawed, adding to pressure on the Australian government over its AI and intellectual property policy.

ip_further_links.title: Australian creative sector launches campaign against unauthorised AI use of copyright material
ip_further_links.summary: Australian creative industry groups have launched a coordinated public campaign demanding that AI companies obtain consent and provide compensation before using copyrighted material for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Google, Meta, TikTok Oppose Indonesia's AI Copyright Bill
ip_further_links.summary: Major US tech platforms have formally opposed Indonesia's proposed legislation that would require AI companies to seek copyright permission and pay royalties for training data sourced from Indonesian creators.

ip_further_links.title: Will the Real Artist Please Stand Up? Suno Sued Over Elvis and Eminem Music.
ip_further_links.summary: Suno faces additional copyright claims alleging its AI music generator produced outputs substantially similar to recordings by Elvis Presley and Eminem, widening the legal challenges against the company.

ip_further_links.title: 'Not simply a UK copyright issue': A US perspective on Getty v Stability AI
ip_further_links.summary: Legal commentary from a US perspective argues that the Getty v Stability AI appeal in the UK has significant implications beyond British copyright law, with potential influence on how US courts approach similar AI training disputes.

ip_further_links.title: CJEU follows AG Opinion and rules that the authorization under Article 17(1) of the DSM Directive also covers acts of reproduction
ip_further_links.summary: The Court of Justice of the EU has ruled that the authorisation granted under Article 17(1) of the Digital Single Market Directive extends to acts of reproduction, clarifying the scope of copyright obligations for online platforms.

ip_further_links.title: AI in the patent industry: Have you read the terms and conditions?
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat examines how AI tools are being adopted in the patent industry and raises concerns about whether practitioners are scrutinising the IP ownership and confidentiality terms embedded in AI service agreements.
